events.name: January 1974
events.note: January 1974: days of rain from Cyclone Wanda on soaked ground, and the Brisbane River backing up Oxley Creek (about 10.3 m, worked out from the 5.45 m peak at the city gauge).

events.name: January 2011
events.note: January 2011: mostly the Brisbane River backing up Oxley Creek (about 9.3 m, from the 4.46 m peak at the city gauge), with ordinary rain here.

events.name: February 2022
events.note: February 2022: record rain on soaked ground, with the creeks and the river backing up Oxley Creek (about 8.7 m, from the 3.85 m peak at the city gauge).

events.name: 1% AEP flood
events.note: A 1 in 100 chance in any year: the Bureau's 1% design storm on Moorooka (97 mm in an hour, 144 mm in three), or a river flood like 2011, whichever is higher.

events.name: 2% AEP flood
events.note: A 1 in 50 chance in any year: the Bureau's 2% design storm (87 mm in an hour), or the matching river flood.

events.name: 5% AEP flood
events.note: A 1 in 20 chance in any year: the Bureau's 5% design storm (74 mm in an hour), or the matching river flood.

events.name: 0.2% AEP flood
events.note: A 1 in 500 chance in any year: the Bureau's rare-rainfall storm (129 mm in an hour), or a river flood above 1974's.

sources: Our own flood simulation: terrain and buildings (c) State of Queensland, CC BY 4.0; design rainfall (c) Bureau of Meteorology (2016 IFDs for Moorooka); river levels worked out from the Bureau's recorded Brisbane City gauge peaks. A guide only: no council flood mapping is used.
